newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada urges that Zaire mission continue.
newsitem.headline: Canada urges that Zaire mission continue.

text.p: Canada urged on Sunday that the multinational humanitarian aid mission to central Africa continue despite the massive movement of refugees from Zaire back into Rwanda.
"Now is not the time to pause and reflect. We still have to have very direct action," Canadian Foreign Affairs Minister Lloyd Axworthy told Reuters.

"We're not saying that it will be exactly as we envisioned it two or three days ago because clearly the refugee movement alters that, but it doesn't mean to say that the international presence or involvement no longer is necessary," he said.
Axworthy said the international commitment to help the estimated 1.2 million refugees that were in Zaire helped spur the flood of refugees back to Rwanda over the last three days.
The movement of an estimated 400,000 refugees across the border into Rwanda since Friday has raised questions about the need for the Canadian-led multinational force.

But Axworthy said large numbers of refugees remain in various parts of eastern Zaire, and their weakened physical condition and other factors may be making it difficult for them to join the exodus. Although the international mission might be modified, contributing countries should not abandon it, he said.

"To stop now might affect that (refugee movement) in the wrong way and therefore I think we have to continue to make sure there is an international presence, international involvement. If we have to modifiy it (the mission), fine," Axworthy said.

Canadian officials said on Sunday that Lt. Gen. Maurice Baril, commander of the multinational force, would leave Ottawa for Kigali, Rwanda late on Sunday night. Once there, he would assess the changing refugee situation in Zaire and Rwanda.

"We think that we still have to go there and determine exactly what kind of assistance and support is still required. There are a lot of conflicting reports, lots of things are changing," Axworthy said.
A contingent of 117 Canadian military reconnaissance personnel left the airbase in Trenton, Ontario at 3:13 p.m. EST (2013 GMT) on Sunday on an Airbus jet bound for Kigali.

After an estimated 20-hour flight via Ancona, Italy, the contingent would join a group of 34 Canadian reconnaissance personnel who were given permission by Rwanda earlier on Sunday to leave Kigali airport, where they had been detained for almost a day.

Axworthy said that aside from helping Rwandan refugees leave Zaire, Canadian military personnel, the Disaster Assistance Response Team (DART) in particular, could play a role in helping refugees resettle in Rwanda.

The minister said he will be conferring in Ottawa on Monday with the ambassadors of African countries and those developed nations contributing to the relief effort. A meeting of officials from those countries involved or affected also has been scheduled for Wednesday in Stuttgart, Germany.

Canada also said on Sunday that it was providing C$15 million ($11.3 million) in new emergency aid to refugees in the central African region. The humanitarian aid includes support for Canadian medical personnel, engineers and logistics experts organised by the Canadian Red Cross and other relief agencies.
